purpose: Teach: すてき/好ん/呟い/見失っ/うまかっ/脱ぎ/日当たり/当っ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、ばあさんのお着物、すてきだったぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when you were young, your kimono was so beautiful.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle gaze into the middle distance. Warm but wistful — the voice of someone holding onto a memory with tenderness. Unhurried pace.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃんは漬物を好んで召し上がったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather always did love his pickles, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Slightly dreamy, talking through layers of time. A small, knowing smile in the voice. Tender without sadness. Pace is unhurried, almost conversational with her own past.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お祖母ちゃんがお歌を呟いてたぞ
lines.en: And when you were young, Gran used to hum songs to herself.
lines.style: Voice softens further. Eyes closed for a moment. Speaking almost to himself — remembering the sound of her voice in their old home. Gentle, deliberate pacing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦争中、お父様を見失った話されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather talked about losing your father during the war, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: A pause before speaking, as if choosing which memory to hold. Tender but grounded — not escaping into sadness. Voice steady and present. Slight questioning lilt at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、ばあさんのお料理、うまかったぞ
lines.en: Your cooking back then, Gran — it was always so good.
lines.style: Warmth and appreciation in the opening. Voice lingers on the memory like tasting it again. Quiet satisfaction. Slow, savoring pace. Small, contented exhale at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お風呂上りに浴衣をお脱ぎになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather would slip out of his yukata after his bath, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Affectionate amusement beneath the surface. A small, private recollection. Voice is warm and understanding — these are the small, living details she holds. Gentle, unhurried.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃のお家は日当たり良かったぞ
lines.en: Your old house got such lovely sunlight, didn't it.
lines.style: Quiet wonder. Opens with gentle recognition — a visual memory. Pace is reflective, almost meditative. Voice trails slightly at the end, as if looking out a window from long ago.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃんの予想がよく当ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather's hunches were usually right, weren't they, dear?
lines.style: Warm acknowledgment mixed with gentle pride. Voice carries both admiration and the intimacy of knowing someone deeply. Pace is easy and familiar, like confirming something she's always known.
